doc.title: Josiah "Cie" Frazier and Alfred Williams Interview, 1961-01-18

title: Stick position and ending rolls with the bass drum
summary: After an offer of fruitcake, Cie wants a few more slow and crush rolls. Williams explains keeping the sticks close and counting four beats on the bass drum to come out of a roll.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: I tried to cross! By the way I had some fruitcake if you'd like a piece of fruitcake with it! No!

Something to kill your appetite! I know you're going to be a little longer than me! Look I'll tell you! Look I'll just do a couple more of them slow rolls and crush rolls and... ! Yeah! Just check that! Yeah! Just remember to keep my hands out here!

Yeah! Well if you want to do it while you're playing but I know that you pull some bands! Yeah! I'll just pull my back! I'll give it a bit! With your drums! A long time you find it's more easier for you if you keep your position of your stick like that and you can get the tire quick if you keep it close like that! Yeah! Because your hands play around! Yeah! Then you couldn't make whatever you... It's that way! It's that way! It's playing down! See for the benefit of your drum playing all the time try to practice that hand be like I tell you like on this shape playing your drum at all times! Yeah! And you can make it! With all your stuff you can always reach out with your left hand and hit it! Yeah! Yeah! Yeah! Yeah! Yeah! Yeah! Yeah! Yeah! Yeah! Yeah! Yeah! Yeah! Yeah! Yeah! Yeah! Yeah! Yeah! Yeah! Yeah! Yeah! Yeah. And you notice how to end that roll. Oakland One, two, one, two, one.
When you know that you might have to go forward. When you have to make you... You see? They help you up like this. They help you up. They help you up when you play this.
They give you more guys, they put four beats on your bass drum.
I guess you could make it an eight if you wanted to. If you want to make it, yeah. It would go, say, in four and then eight. It wouldn't play no sixes or anything.

No, no, no four. You're counting four. You're playing a slow tempo. You see, if you're talking to get puzzles, just count four beats on your bass drum, same time you're rolling that drum, and then that'll bring you out on one ball. In that tempo you're playing it. If you're playing a fast tempo, it's the same thing.
Let me try this. Let's try this. Try a four and then an eight.
You want me to do something on the drum?
